This is a proposed zoning map amendment and there's no development proposal associated with the application.
The applicant is indicated their reason for the application is due to the existing B3 zoning that does limit redevelopment and potential of these properties.
And they're seeking certainty on expanded development opportunities for their properties for future development through this rezoning to be six.
The purpose of the B3 district is to facilitate arterial commercial development providing a moderate to wide range of commercial uses on small to medium sized lots.
Generally B3 can be considered as a low density arterial commercial zone.
The purpose of the B3 B6 district part of me is to facilitate a wide range of commercial institutional and residential uses in a high density form in the downtown area.
B6 is the primary zone in our downtown and it supports mixed uses in a flexible high density form.
Now in comparison comparing the two zones outlined on the slide, B6 is a more appropriate fit for the urban context of downtown and the land uses building forms and densities that are desired.
Just a note on some of the relevant policy context, notably the official community plan and city center plan which both provide guidance to us in considering this application.
Firstly, the OCP identifies all land within our downtown for high density mixed use development that includes residential commercial institutional recreational cultural and community uses.
Further, the city center plan from 2013 did identify improvements to the western edge of downtown as being a priority.
That plan cited the large surface parking areas, the poor pedestrian environment and negative perception is an entry point to downtown.
That plan subsequently identified a review of the zoning of the west downtown area as an implementation action.
As noted, the subject sites are located within the district core of the proposed downtown event and entertainment district.
The district core is outlined by the small dash line on the slide which identifies properties that are adjacent to or interfacing with the catalyst facilities and their surrounding public realm.
Where there's a particular interesting and considering how development on these sites will interface with or relate to the future facilities.
So administration is currently working on the district plan for the deed as part of an updated city center plan, which will clarify the objectives for this area as it redevelops.
Development of a new zoning district for land within the district core has been identified as part of this work.
This new zone will implement standards to ensure appropriate land use and facilitate high quality design that integrates with the public realm.
In general, well, it's very early in terms of a new zone and its development.
It's expected that the new zone would provide for high density mixed use development similar to the B6 district, both regulations that are tailored to the context and objectives for the area.
It's expected that the district plan will be brought forward for city councils consideration in August or September of this year.
An implemented implementation of the new zone and rezoning of a associated land is expected in 2025.

In addition to this work on the district plan, the conceptual design for the deed project including the event and convention center facilities and surrounding public realm was released earlier this year.
This design shown on the screen in plan view illustrates how the Wall Street properties will directly interface with the proposed event center site and surrounding public realm.

The design here envisions this space between the properties and the event center is a high quality support street that provides service access for the adjacent facilities and properties will also being a functional and inviting space.

The administration agrees that the B6 district is a generally appropriate choice for these properties and that B3 does not support development options that are desirable in a downtown context.

However, the primary concern with this application is its timing amid a significant planning exercise that will set the direction for the area through the district plan and ahead of consideration of a new zoning district for lands within this area.
We feel that to rezoning to be 6 in the interim would be out of step with this work and as there is still uncertainty around the final outcomes of the district plan and its objectives.
As well as the expectations for land use and built form that will be articulated through the new zone.
Our report does expand on a couple specific risks of rezoning to be 6 in the interim, which includes firstly the current lack of appropriate regulations for active interface.
Between future development on these sites and the events center site immediately to the east.
Second, the B6 regulations happen to currently permit surface parking as a permitted use so that uses permitted as a right.

We do see service parking acknowledging that that's not necessarily the owner's intent or the applicant's intent.
We do see service parking in the risk of such as being counterproductive to the type of urban environment essential for a vibrant district.
So we are planning to take a restrictive approach that form of development in this area.

There is a significant planning process underway for the area that includes these sites and to rezoned in the interim will not be prudent.
Indeed project if it proceeds with constitute a significant public investment immediately adjacent to these properties and given the importance of such a project to downtown and the city is a whole.

We feel there's a necessity for us to approach approach the planning for the area in a coherent way where decisions on the overall vision and objectives for the area and the specific zoning treatment of surrounding properties are made in an appropriate sequence.

We are actively working towards the certainty and expanded development potential that these property owners desire through this application and we know their applications made with good intentions to contribute positively to the downtown with their properties in the future.

We are not recommending refusal of the application because we disagree with expanding development potential in the sites rather we simply have a different perspective on the timing and means to that end.
The time is needed for us to have new zoning ready to put in place for these and other properties in the area.
